newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS ACCEPTS ZOELLER'S APOLOGY FOR REMARKS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS ACCEPTS ZOELLER'S APOLOGY FOR REMARKS.

text.p: Tiger Woods chided Fuzzy Zoeller for making an unfortunate stab at humour but on Thursday accepted his apology for remarks made following Woods's triumph at the Masters Tournament two weeks ago.

In a CNN television interview done on Masters Sunday but aired a week later, Zoeller referred to Woods as "that little boy" and suggested the 21-year-old runaway winner of the Masters not have fried chicken or collard greens served for next year's champions dinner.
"At first I was shocked to hear that Fuzzy Zoeller had made these unfortunate remarks," Woods said in a statement issued by his management representative in Los Angeles.
"His attempt at humour was out of bounds, and I was disappointed by it.

"But having played golf with Fuzzy, I know he is a jokester; and I have concluded that no personal animosity toward me was intended. I respect Fuzzy as a golfer and as a person and for the many good things he has done for others throughout his career. I know he feels badly about his remarks. We all make mistakes, and it is time to move on.
"I accept Fuzzy's apology and hope everyone can now put this behind us."

Woods became the youngest winner of the Masters and the first black golfer to win a major championship with a spectacular performance in which he set an Augusta National scoring record and won by the largest margin ever.
Zoeller's remarks drew a storm of criticism and cost him his longtime sponsorship deal with the the Kmart discount department store chain.

Zoeller, a 24-year veteran of the PGA Tour and winner of the 1979 Masters, issued a public apology on Monday. On Wednesday he withdrew from the Greater Greensboro Chrysler Classic tournament saying he needed to "make things right with Tiger" before he would play in any tournament.

In the interview broadcast on CNN's "Pro Golf Weekly" show, Zoeller said: "That little boy is driving well and he's putting well. He's doing everything it takes to win. So, you know what you guys do when he gets in here? You pat him on the back and say, 'Congratulations' and, 'Enjoy it' and tell him not to serve fried chicken next year."
Zoeller then snapped his fingers, turned to walk away, and added, "Or collard greens or whatever the hell they serve."
